## Experience

::: {.cv-row}
**New York Genome Center** · Computational Biology · New York, NY
[Aug 2023 – present]{.meta}
:::

[Senior Bioinformatics Analyst, Nov 2026 – present · Bioinformatics Analyst, Aug 2023 – Oct 2026]{.meta}

Transcriptomic analysis and research across cancer, neurodegenerative, and autoimmune disease. I work with researchers at NYGC and partner institutions to design, analyze, and interpret studies, and I help bring machine learning tools into that work.

- Helped build **DECONVersation** at NYGC with fellow researchers, a deconvolution method that uses embeddings from single-cell foundation models (Geneformer, Cell2Sentence, scGPT, scVI) to estimate cell-type proportions from bulk RNA-seq. It matches or outperforms MuSiC, DWLS, and BayesPrism across benchmark datasets. First-author preprint, presented at MLCB 2025.
- Benchmarked single-cell foundation models against scVI, Harmony, and PCA for dimensionality reduction, batch correction, and representation learning, setting the group's model-selection criteria for single-cell pipelines.
- Led transcriptomic analysis for the NYGC ALS Consortium: differential expression and cell-type composition across brain and spinal cord regions, linked to genetic and clinical features.
- Built perturbation-analysis pipelines for CRISPR functional genomics data across HPC (Slurm) and cloud environments.
- Designed reusable NGS workflows for bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and spatial transcriptomics supporting biomarker discovery and target identification.
- Established the group's single-cell QC and benchmarking framework, with automated metrics, doublet and ambient-RNA handling, and versioned reference data.
- Built interactive R Shiny and D3.js applications, including the public [ALS Gene Browser](https://alsbrowser.nygenome.org/), so collaborators can explore results without writing code.

::: {.cv-row}
**EMD Serono (Merck KGaA)** · Bioinformatics Intern, Machine Learning · Billerica, MA
[Feb 2023 – Jul 2023]{.meta}
:::

- Prepared multi-omic data (expression, DNA methylation, somatic mutations, copy number) and built a cancer-agnostic machine learning model to classify the tumor microenvironment into subtypes.
- Mapped model predictions to clinical variables, including patient survival and response to immunotherapy.
- Compared XGBoost, random forest, and neural network classifiers with nested cross-validation and SHAP-based interpretation.
- Delivered model evaluation and documentation covering accuracy, interpretability, and clinical applicability.

- Identified colorectal cancer subtype-associated gene modules with WGCNA and characterized their pathway and GO enrichment.
- Analyzed scRNA-seq and CITE-seq data to quantify drug-treatment effects at single-cell resolution.
- Developed and validated logistic regression classifiers for colorectal cancer subtypes.

::: {.cv-row}
**Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine** · Machine Learning Intern · Berlin, Germany
[May 2021 – Aug 2021]{.meta}
:::

- Designed a variational autoencoder for joint representation of multi-omic colorectal cancer data (expression, copy number, methylation).
- Implemented a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to align distributions across data modalities.
- Showed that the learned embeddings predict survival and drug response across colorectal cancer subtypes.

## Skills

**Machine learning.** Deep learning (VAEs, autoencoders, transformers); single-cell foundation models (scVI, scGPT, Geneformer, Cell2Sentence); representation learning, batch correction, transfer learning; XGBoost, random forests, SVM, regularized regression; clustering, PCA/UMAP; model evaluation and interpretability (SHAP).

**Frameworks.** PyTorch, scikit-learn, Hugging Face Transformers, scanpy, scvi-tools, Seurat, DESeq2, limma, edgeR, WGCNA, QIIME 2, pandas, NumPy, tidyverse.

**Genomics data.** Bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, CITE-seq, ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, CRISPR screens, WGS/WES, DNA methylation, CNV, 16S rRNA.

**Engineering.** Python, R, SQL, Bash, Java; Nextflow, Snakemake, WDL; Docker, Git; Slurm/HPC, AWS, GCP.

**Communication.** R Shiny, D3.js, interactive dashboards, technical writing, presenting to bench and clinical scientists.
